worked_solution:
The substitution $z={y}^{-3}$ transforms the given equation into the equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+\frac{6}{x}z=-\frac{9}{{x}^{2}}.
$$

The above equation is in the standard form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x)
$$

with

$$
P(x)=\frac{6}{x},\,Q(x)=-\frac{9}{{x}^{2}}\,.
$$

We then compute an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(x) & ={e}^{\int P(x)\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{\int 6/x\,\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{6\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡{x}^{6}} \\  & ={x}^{6}\end{aligned}
$$

under the condition that $x>0.$

Multiplying both sides of the equation in standard form by $I(x)={x}^{6}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{6}\cdot (\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+\frac{6}{x}\,z) & ={x}^{6}\cdot (-\frac{9}{{x}^{2}}) \\ {x}^{6}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+6{x}^{5}z & =-9{x}^{4} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{x}^{6}z] & =-9{x}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[{x}^{6}z]\,\text{d}x & =\int -9{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\ {x}^{6}z & =-\frac{9}{5}{x}^{5}+{C}_{1} \\ z & =\frac{C-9{x}^{5}}{5{x}^{6}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=5{C}_{1}.$

Next, we determine $y(x)$ by writing $z={y}^{-3}.$ This results in

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{-3} & =\frac{C-9{x}^{5}}{5{x}^{6}} \\ {y}^{3} & =\frac{5{x}^{6}}{C-9{x}^{5}} \\ y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{5{x}^{6}}{C-9{x}^{5}}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

From the initial condition  $y(1)=\frac{1}{2}$ we determine $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{5}{C-9}} \\ \frac{1}{8} & =\frac{5}{C-9} \\ C-9 & =40 \\ C & =49.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{5{x}^{6}}{49-9{x}^{5}}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
